model: Organic score = 100 x listed x findable x reach. listed: 1 live, 0.5 PR/submission pending, 0.3-0.2 blocked on a human/CI step, 0 skipped/not published. findable for registry-backed surfaces is MEASURED via fully-paginated /v0/servers?search=<token> calls (limit=100, cursor loop -- fixes a prior single-page undercount risk): p(seen|query) = 0 if our current-version row for THAT server does not appear, else min(1, 10/rank), using the row's own best rank restricted to that server's registry name(s) (a token like 'price' that also substring-matches a different server's long slug, e.g. office-suite, is NOT credited to the wrong server). findable = mean of p over 56 natural query slots across all nine servers' query_set (was 41 across six servers before currency/docx/timezone existed). Per-server organic = 100 x mean(p) over that server's own query set. 'Hosted endpoints' findable = share of the 56 query slots whose matched row belongs to a server that now carries a non-empty remotes[] (8 of 9 servers: everything except office-suite). fleet.fleet_score is a noisy-OR over the nine per-server organics (100 x (1 - product(1 - p_i/100))), applied identically before and after for comparability.

fleet.verdict: Three new servers (currency, docx, timezone) shipped since ORGANIC_R2, all live and hosted; office-suite -- previously unpublished and worth 0 -- is now live too, though still stdio-only. Registry findable rose from 0.276 to 0.345 (36 of 56 tokens matched, up from 22 of 41) even though the denominator grew by 15 tokens, because the three new servers all landed on multiple near-empty tokens the way expense-tracker did last time: timezone alone is now the fleet's strongest server (organic 79.7, ahead of expense-tracker's 66.7) on the back of rank-1-of-3 on 'slots' and 'world-clock'. fleet_score (noisy-OR across nine server organics) moved from 90.1 to 99.2 -- it is now close to its ceiling because at least one server (timezone) is reliably findable on several near-empty tokens, and noisy-OR only needs one strong server. Hosted-endpoints findable nearly doubled (0.317 to 0.607) because expense-tracker and spreadsheet both picked up remotes[] since the last pass -- office-suite is now the only stdio-only server left. The real bottleneck moved off naming and onto distribution mechanics: awesome-mcp-servers is now explicitly CI-blocked pending a Glama listing that is itself blocked (crawler-only intake, no manual add without an account), and neither Smithery nor Glama show any presence at all despite 9 published .mcpb bundles. Release downloads grew +79 in under 2 hours, the first real download signal recorded for this fleet -- direction unconfirmed (could be our own re-checks/CI, not necessarily third-party installs).
